45	CASE OD2-DEV-CONFOUND: The tutoring program whose students score lower
46	
47	Setting: Pellham Ridge Unified School District (fictional) runs five middle schools (Ashgrove, Corliss, Dunmore, Fenwick, Halvard) with about 3,100 students in grades 6–8. Since October 2025 it has run Bridge Hours, an after-school small-group math tutoring program staffed by a contractor, Northgate Learning Partners, at a cost of $640,000 a year. The board votes on 12 March 2026 whether to renew, cut or expand the Northgate contract. A new board dashboard compares winter benchmark scores of Bridge Hours participants with those of non-participants.
48	
49	Presenting request: Superintendent Abel Kruger: 'Trustee Venter will move to end Bridge Hours at the March 12 budget meeting because the dashboard shows participants scoring far below everyone else. Northgate says the program is working and wants it expanded. I need to know what that score gap actually means and what I should recommend to the board.'
50	
51	INITIAL EVIDENCE
52	E1 [stage S1] Email from Trustee Marisol Venter to the superintendent and board, 2 Feb 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: Bridge Hours. The winter benchmark dashboard settles this. Bridge Hours students averaged 198.0; everyone else averaged 224.4. That's a 26-point gap, and it shows up at every one of our five middle schools. We are paying Northgate $640,000 a year for a program whose students do worse than kids who never set foot in it. Teachers tell me the tutors teach tricks that contradict what's taught in class. At the March 12 budget meeting I will move that we end the Northgate contract and return the money to the general fund.
53	E2 [stage S1] Board dashboard, Grade 6–8 Math, winter benchmark (system-record): Board Dashboard — Grade 6–8 Math, Winter Benchmark (administered 12–16 Jan 2026). Bridge Hours participants: n=412, mean scale score 198.0. Non-participants: n=2,694, mean 224.4. Gap (participants minus non-participants) by school: Ashgrove −23.0; Corliss −29.1; Dunmore −22.6; Fenwick −27.4; Halvard −28.7. Proficient (scale ≥ 220): participants 9%, non-participants 58%. Footnote: 'Participant' = enrolled in Bridge Hours on 1 Dec 2025. Scale range 140–300. All students in a grade took the same winter form.
54	E3 [stage S1] Bridge Hours Program Overview 2025–26, district website (document): Bridge Hours offers small-group math tutoring (up to five students per tutor) for grades 6–8 at all five middle schools. Sessions run Tuesdays and Thursdays, 3:35–4:35 p.m., after the 3:15 dismissal bell, from 14 October to 30 April. Tutors are employed by Northgate Learning Partners under contract and use Northgate's 'Stepwise' lesson sets. Students join through school referral; families must return a consent form. A late bus takes participants home. Contact your school's Bridge Hours site coordinator for details.
55	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, grade 7 math teacher, Corliss Middle, taken by a board aide, 28 Jan 2026 (staff-account): 'Two or three of my Bridge kids came back comparing fractions by cross-multiplying when I'd taught common denominators, and one mixed the two methods up on the December quiz. I mentioned it to the tutor; she said they show both ways.' Asked whether Bridge Hours was hurting scores: 'I honestly couldn't say. The kids in Bridge are mostly the ones I was already worried about in September, so I'd expect them to be lower either way. Some of them do seem more willing to try now.'
56	E5 [stage S1] Email from Renata Osei, Regional Director, Northgate Learning Partners, to the superintendent, 3 Feb 2026 (vendor-account): Our tracking shows Bridge Hours students gained 15 scale points from the fall diagnostic to the winter benchmark, versus 9 points for non-participants — roughly two-thirds more growth. The dashboard's raw comparison is unfair to the program. We recommend expanding Bridge Hours to grades 4–5 next year. We would also suggest ending the district's referral list and opening sign-up to any interested student, which would give a more representative picture of what Bridge Hours can achieve.

67	X9 [stage S1] Bridge Hours session attendance logs, 14 Oct – 18 Dec 2025 - source: Northgate attendance system export (log) - file: evidence/X9.txt
68	X10 [stage S1] Spring 2025 state math test results for students enrolled in Bridge Hours in 2025–26 - source: District data warehouse extract, 9 Feb 2026 (system-record) - file: evidence/X10.txt

75	H3: Conflicts between Northgate's Stepwise methods and classroom methods are depressing participants' benchmark scores to some degree.
76	H4: Bridge Hours sessions take time away from participants' regular math instruction.

5	Winter means by fall-diagnostic band, participants (P) vs non-participants (N). Below 180: P n=161, 190.1; N n=118, 191.7. 180–195: P n=213, 201.5; N n=210, 203.8. 196–210: P n=31, 209.9; N n=604, 213.0. Above 210: P n=7 (not reported); N n=1,762, 233.0. This design cannot detect a small Bridge Hours effect in either direction. A comparison of students just either side of the 196 cut can be ready by 27 Feb. Session attendance has not been linked to scores.

input.brief: The score gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. District rules send every student below the 40th percentile on the fall test into the program. Of participants, 91% scored below that line in the fall, against 12% of non-participants. Their fall average was 182.8 versus 215.1. Once students are compared with others who started at similar fall scores, the gap shrinks to a few points. Most of that is explained by the starting difference. Growth is also about equal within each band. The vendor's claim of faster growth is the same effect: low scorers grow more whoever they are. So the dashboard doesn't show the program hurting students. It doesn't show the program working either. The research office says its comparison can't detect a small effect either way. The teacher's concern about conflicting methods is plausible but untested. I'm fairly sure of the selection explanation and unsure about the program's true effect. Don't end the contract on the raw chart, don't expand it, and don't open sign-up to anyone. That would dilute the targeting and make later comparisons harder. Replace the raw chart with the matched comparison before March 12. Get the research office's cut-line comparison, due 27 Feb. Have the math coordinator observe sessions. Link attendance to scores. Then decide on renewal, probably a conditional one.
